rationale: Selected boundary: execution_plan scope, group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb, whose only call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (target project.invoke, phase run) is the complete accumulated training step. The replacement reproduces adapter.run verbatim -- identical optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True), identical no_sync schedule (3 of 4 microbatches), identical model(input_ids=tokens, labels=tokens, use_cache=False).loss / total forward, identical loss.backward(), loss.detach() bookkeeping, torch.stack(losses).sum() inside the gradient_accumulation phase, optimizer.step() + torch.cuda.synchronize() inside the optimizer_step phase (same kernel_optimizer.project.discovery phase contexts), and the same {'loss': step_loss, 'microbatch_losses': torch.stack(losses)} return -- and inserts exactly one dist.barrier(group=state['control_group']) after the final microbatch's forward and immediately before its backward. Measured facts motivating this (inputs/observations, revision de4d95e2): the objective is the max-rank sum of the 13 fp32 SUM allreduce NCCL kernel durations (calls d0938de87369efd500322679 x12 at 28,351,488 B and b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b x1 at 157,541,376 B); collective_calibration measures near-wire completion at these exact sizes (~34.4 ms synthetic total); execution_timeline shows the late rank pays essentially that floor (35.35-35.41 ms) while the early rank pays 53.6-54.3 ms with its first ncclDevKernel_AllReduce spinning 13.7-14.6 ms; cross_rank submit bounds show the early rank's CPU submits all 13 allreduces 12.5-12.9 ms earlier, with the offset already established at the first collective (seq 21) and flat through seq 33 -- i.e. accumulated before the final backward begins, during the 3 unsynchronized no_sync microbatches and the final forward, not during the collective window and not wire time. Mechanism under test: the gloo barrier resets the accumulated inter-rank CPU submission offset at the last host-side point before the 13 allreduce launches, so both ranks' allreduce submissions (and, in this host-bound step where GPU queues stay shallow, their kernel starts) arrive nearly together and the early rank's in-kernel spin collapses from the pre-established offset to residual backward-prefix drift plus per-bucket jitter. Expected effect: max-rank communication_kernel_sum_ms falls from reference ~39.7 ms toward the late-rank near-wire level ~35.5-37 ms (~3-4 ms); this is a hypothesis, not a guaranteed win -- if a share of the clean offset is GPU-side execution-rate asymmetry, only the CPU share is recovered, and the paired MAD-derived noise bounds (1.68/4.85 ms last evaluation) must be exceeded. step_ms safety: the late rank never waits at the barrier (it arrives last); the early rank's barrier wait equals the lead it had accumulated and overlaps GPU execution of the already-submitted final forward kernels, replacing NCCL in-kernel spinning that was already on its wall clock (step ends with torch.cuda.synchronize(), so the step critical path stays the late rank's); measured step_ms 103-107 ms has ample headroom under the 121.51 ms limit (1.05x baseline). Correctness: no numeric kernel is added, removed or reordered; the barrier runs on the gloo control group created in prepare() and already used by before_run(), launches no NCCL kernel, registers no communication hook, and does not touch the DDP reducer, bucket layout (bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True), collective count, payloads, gradients or parameters, so the exact cross-rank gradient replica check (atol=rtol=0), the serial-reference gradient/parameter checks, finite loss and the negative control pass unchanged. Synchronization/state lifecycle: the barrier executes unconditionally on every invocation in every mode (quality, measure, profile) and identically on both ranks (one barrier per run() call, before any allreduce), so repeats, continuous_steps, reset() (state_dict reload), and the separately profiled objective invocations remain safe and symmetric; it cannot deadlock because no rank can skip it (fall back paths are selected identically from rank-shared state) and it performs no CUDA work. Previous feedback repair: the prior candidate (trial-2eafcccfdb, host-lean bitwise-identical GPT2Block composite) passed quality and coverage but scored 40.12 vs reference 39.70 (paired_gain_not_above_noise) and its after-capture still showed a 10.3-12.6 ms submit offset -- symmetric host speedups shrink both ranks' dispatch and leave the relative offset intact; this attempt therefore does not touch host speed at all and instead removes the offset directly at the point where it becomes NCCL in-kernel spin. Route labels are reported via context['record_route'] inside the replacement: distributed:gloo_control_barrier_before_final_backward on the barrier path, fallback:no_control_group_parent_step when the control group is absent/single-rank/dist is uninitialized (exact parent semantics via the reference), and fallback:setup_guard_parent_step when the build-time structural guard fails. The two allreduce call IDs d0938de87369efd500322679 and b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b are affected (their kernel durations are the objective) but are not replacement sites; no inner call is eliminated.
setup_work: build() only inspects context (targets/references/state) and creates Python closures: no CUDA work, no tensor allocation, no parameter transformation, no process-group creation (the barrier reuses state['control_group'] created by prepare()), no module.forward wrapping and no communication hook. Setup allocation delta is 0 bytes and setup time is the module import plus closure creation (sub-millisecond); the first barrier participates in the timed/profiled step semantics exactly like before_run's existing gloo barrier and adds no persistent memory. There are no retained pools, no captured graphs and no cached outputs; every invocation executes the full workload on current inputs.
quality_risks: Effect-size risk (performance, not correctness): if the clean paired offset has a GPU-side execution-rate component, the barrier recovers only the CPU share and the paired gain may stay within the MAD-derived noise bounds (1.68/4.85 ms last evaluation), repeating paired_gain_not_above_noise; the median-of-3 profiled samples also cannot remove a fresh one-off scheduling stall landing after the barrier.

step_ms risk: the early rank's barrier wait is added to its wall clock; if in some sample the early rank's post-barrier submission tail (its CPU is intrinsically faster) extends past the late rank's completion, step_ms rises slightly; the 103-107 ms measured level leaves ~15 ms of headroom to the 121.51 ms constraint, and the wait replaces allreduce spin already on the same critical path, so a material regression is not expected but is monitored by the constraint check.

Timing-only change: numerics are bit-identical by construction (no numeric op added/removed/reordered), so the exact gradient replica check, serial-reference gradient/parameter checks, finite loss and negative control are unaffected; the residual risk is operational (a rank crashing mid-step before the barrier would make the peer wait at the 120 s gloo timeout), which is the same exposure the parent's before_run barrier and NCCL collectives already have.

Fallback paths run the parent verbatim (recorded as fallback:no_control_group_parent_step / fallback:setup_guard_parent_step), which leaves the objective unchanged rather than incorrect; the barrier path is selected identically from rank-shared state on all ranks, so collective participation cannot diverge.

Diagnostic attribution risk: the barrier adds a CPU-side c10d barrier op to traces; it produces no NCCL kernel, so communication_kernel_sum_ms still sums exactly the 13 DDP allreduce kernels, but timeline interpretations must not credit it with wire-time changes.
